note_text: The 69-year-old right-handed patient presents to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. On questioning, the patient reports some difficulty speaking for 3 months. During conversation, the patient often has difficulty repeating what the interlocutor has said. The patient has hypertension and takes hydrochlorothiazide. Vital signs are within normal limits. The patient speaks fluently in full sentences and demonstrates normal comprehension. When asked to say “kindergarten,” the patient replies, “Sintelmarvin… no, that's wrong…kinterflargin, no that isn't it either...kantolargen...no? How about, kindergarten?” I recommend an ESI triage level of 5 for this patient.

The patient has human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) diagnosed 10 years ago and admits to not always being compliant with antiretroviral medication. The patient reports a 20-pack-year smoking history and no alcohol or recreational drug use. Review of systems is significant for a 6 kg (13.2 lb) unintentional weight loss over the past 2 months. Temperature is 37.8℃ (100.0℉), and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. Right-sided axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy is present. Cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable. Spleen size is 16 cm on percussion. Laboratory studies: hemoglobin 9 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3, leukocyte count 18,000/mm3, platelet count 130,000/mm3, serum creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, and serum lactate dehydrogenase 1,000 U/L.
